skills.name: Value added tax (VAT): calculation and accounting entries

note.text:
VAT in Cameroon is 19.25% of the price excluding tax (HT): 17.5% VAT plus 10% of that as council tax (17.5% × 1.1 = 19.25%).
• Amount including tax (TTC) = HT + VAT = HT × 1.1925.
• On sales, the enterprise charges VAT: credit 443 VAT invoiced (collected).
• On purchases, it pays VAT it can recover: debit 445 VAT recoverable.
• VAT payable to the State = VAT invoiced − VAT recoverable (account 4441). If recoverable is bigger, the difference is a VAT credit (4449), carried forward.

sections.heading: A tax on added value
sections.text:
Value added tax (VAT) is a tax on consumption. Each enterprise charges VAT on its sales and deducts the VAT it paid on its purchases, so in the end the final consumer bears the tax.
In Cameroon the rate is {19.25}%: {17.5}% VAT plus council tax of {10}% of it ({17.5}% × {1.1} = {19.25}%).

sections.heading: Calculating
sections.text:
• HT (hors taxes): price excluding tax.
• VAT = {19.25}% × HT.
• TTC (toutes taxes comprises): HT + VAT = HT × {1.1925}.
For {200000} FCFA HT: VAT = {38500} FCFA and TTC = {238500} FCFA.
To go back from TTC to HT, divide by {1.1925}.

sections.heading: Recording and paying
sections.text:
• Sales: debit {'411'} Customers with TTC; credit {'701'} Sales with HT and {'443'} VAT invoiced with the VAT.
• Purchases: debit {'601'} Purchases with HT and {'445'} VAT recoverable with the VAT; credit {'401'} Suppliers with TTC.
• At the end of the month, VAT payable ({'4441'}) = VAT invoiced − VAT recoverable, paid to the State. If recoverable is bigger, the difference is a VAT credit ({'4449'}) carried to the next month.

key_words.meaning: recoverable VAT larger than invoiced VAT, carried forward

mistake.why: VAT is calculated on the price before tax.

worked_example.problem: Goods are sold for {ht} FCFA HT. Find the VAT and the amount including tax.

cards.idea: VAT = {19.25}% of the price excluding tax.
VAT payable = VAT invoiced − VAT recoverable.

check.prompt: In a month, VAT invoiced on sales is {inv} FCFA and VAT recoverable on purchases is {rec} FCFA. What VAT must be paid to the State (FCFA)? (0 if there is a credit)

misconceptions.explain: Subtract the recoverable VAT from the invoiced VAT.

solution: {inv > rec ? 'Payable: ' + fmt(inv - rec) + ' FCFA.' : 'Recoverable is bigger: no VAT to pay; credit of ' + fmt(rec - inv) + ' FCFA.'}

questions.prompt: Goods worth {ht} FCFA HT are sold. Find the VAT at {19.25}% (FCFA).

misconceptions.explain: That is the amount including tax. VAT is only the tax part.
The rate in Cameroon is {19.25}% ({17.5}% plus council tax).

questions.prompt: Find the amount including tax (TTC) for a sale of {ht} FCFA HT (VAT {19.25}%).

misconceptions.explain: That is the VAT only; add it to the HT amount.

questions.prompt: In a month, VAT invoiced on sales is {inv} FCFA and VAT recoverable on purchases is {rec} FCFA. What VAT must be paid to the State (FCFA)? (0 if there is a credit)

misconceptions.explain: Subtract the recoverable VAT from the invoiced VAT.

solution: {inv > rec ? 'Payable: ' + fmt(inv - rec) + ' FCFA.' : 'Recoverable is bigger: no VAT to pay; credit of ' + fmt(rec - inv) + ' FCFA.'}

pick.q: In a credit sale, which account records the VAT charged to the customer?
e: Cash is not involved in a credit sale.
pick.y: VAT charged on sales is owed to the State.

pick.q: In a credit purchase of goods, which account records the VAT paid to the supplier?
pick.y: The enterprise can deduct this VAT.

pick.q: Which account is debited when goods are sold on credit for an amount including tax?
e: Sales is credited with the HT amount.
pick.y: The customer owes the full TTC amount.

questions.prompt: An invoice shows a total including tax of {ttc} FCFA (VAT {19.25}%). Find the amount excluding tax (FCFA).

misconceptions.explain: Taking {19.25}% of the TTC is wrong: VAT is {19.25}% of the HT. Divide by {1.1925}.
